text:
solstice-cs: Hey team — Solstice.ai seeing huge p99 on embeddings API since ~03:10 UTC. Customer dashboard shows timeouts and 10s+ responses intermittently. Affects /v1/embeddings only and started right after their nightly batch window.

maya-support: Ack, thanks. Can you paste a sample request id + a short repro (no customer PII)? Also can you confirm whether they're using the hosted endpoint or a dedicated pool?

solstice-cs: Hosted. Example request id: req_2053001111_x7. Sample payload (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-16k",
  "input": ["<doc_1>", "<doc_2>", ..., "<doc_6000>"]  // ~6k small docs batched client-side
}
```
We batch client-side into one request (they said to save on request overhead). p95 ~ 120ms but p99 jumped to 8–12s.

aj-eng-sre: Thanks, reproducing in logs now. I see a pattern: giant single-request batches from tenant=solstice.ai are causing the runtime to allocate large KV caches per request and thrash GPU memory. Trace for req_2053001111_x7 shows repeated garbage-collecting of inference cache and kernel fallback logs: 
```
[runtime] alloc-kv: requested 2.4GB -> evicting prefixes (tenant=solstice.ai)
[kernel] quant-fallback: op matmul fallback to CPU (latency spike)
[batcher] head-of-line wait 6.2s (waiting for KV write lock)
```
Appears to be head-of-line blocking: single huge request holds resources and causes small requests to queue; also we get kernel selection fallback under memory pressure.

ryan-runtime: Correlating with metrics: tenant solstice.ai had a sustained 1.2GB/sec token ingress during the 03:00-03:20 window. GPU mem pressure sigma spiked to 92% and our eviction policy started to thrash. Batching latency distribution shows big variance when any request > 1k docs present.

maya-support: Ok. Customer-side mitigation options? Recommend they stop sending massive single-request batches. But we should also provide runway mitigations on our side.

aj-eng-sre: Proposed mitigations (short term -> long term):
- Short-term (5–30m): Create a soft per-tenant request size cap (reject > X docs) and auto-split large requests with a notice. Or route solstice.ai to a reserved mini-pool to isolate their resource usage.
- Medium-term (hours): Add per-tenant concurrency limits + max_batch_size enforcement in ingress layer.
- Long-term (weeks): Prefix/KV memory accounting improvements + proactive kernel selection to avoid CPU fallback under pressure.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-2053 and attached current traces.

maya-support: I'm going to ask for temporary reservation. @aj-eng-sre can you spin a small dedicated pool (1xA10x8) and pin tenant to it for the next 2 hours? That should drop cross-tenant tail impact. Also add a per-tenant allowlist for burst capacity so we can safely reserve without changing their config.

aj-eng-sre: On it. Spawning pool now. Command run:
```
rbctl reservation create --tenant solstice.ai --pool small-embed-resv --gpu a10x8 --duration 2h --priority burst
```
ETA ~4m. After reservation up, I'll add a transient routing rule: route requests with header X-Tenant: solstice.ai -> small-embed-resv.

deploy-bot: reservation small-embed-resv status: provisioning -> active (2053001390).

aj-eng-sre: Routing rule applied. Also pushed a temporary ingress guard to reject single-request batches > 2500 docs with HTTP 429 + guidance. Rule id: guard-2053-01.

solstice-cs: Thanks — customer applied a temporary client-side change to split batches as well (they shipped a small client rollback). Early numbers look better.

ryan-runtime: After routing to reserved pool, p99 for other tenants dropped from 11s -> 220ms within one minute. Solstice.ai p99 improved to ~700ms (we still see some residual CPU fallback traces for a few requests).

maya-support: Customer happy for now. We'll keep reservation for 2h and collect traces + a reproducible test case for runtime team.

aj-eng-sre: Next steps / owners: 
- aj-eng-sre: validate no regression from reservation and collect heap+KV accounting snapshot (due 2053002000).
- ryan-runtime: synth load test that reproduces eviction scenario and file a runbook (due 2053003600).
- maya-support: coordinate with Solstice CS to enforce client-side batch limits (done) and request a sample of production batch sizes (due 2053002500).
- platform: consider adding per-tenant quota enforcement (RFC) — assign to eng-platform backlog.

solstice-cs: We'll send sample logs and confirm if further spikes occur. Really appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:.

aj-eng-sre: Marking this thread resolved for now. If we still see kernel quant fallback after the reservation expires, we'll re-open and escalate to runtime perf.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2053 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
